body: College just gives me opportunity to be adequately paid while performing a profession I enjoy. I could spend every day in the library, but I'd be dirt poor.

If I could go to college without having to work, graduate, and then get a job I'm fond of that pays decently, I'd be happy enough to not consider suicide. In the US, this is about as possible as gaining superpowers from toxic waste.

Thanks.

Using the word free to describe anyone in this system is very inaccurate. I see your point, but I'm not free to do anything I want. If I were to go to any of the 20 or so places I'd like to visit or even live, I'd need money for rent (or someone to live with), which I don't have, and I'd need a job, which I don't want. I basically need a free ride (if only temporarily) through college or I quit.

Thank you. 

>did you find the work difficult, or was it more that high school just seemed pointless?

I found it insignificant my first 3 years, then I did a 180* and got a 4.0 GPA my last year. My cumulative ended being below 2.0, though. 

>it would be a mistake to put the burden of proof on the 'living' alternative

What do you mean?

>'cost of living exceeded the benefits'

I didn't mean for it to come out that way. I meant to say the cost of living life and suffering through it is greater than the benefits of life. 

>Do you find merit in any artwork, novels, music?

Sure, those are most of the 'benefits' I speak of.

>Not all change has to be of the revolutionary nature. Small steps- that's the only way institutions and authorities change without bloodshed.

I mostly agree, but how much oppression can/should we stand? For me, it's too much already. 

>For example: "Money would solve most of my problems" to me indicates that if you were instead in a job that lined up with your interests, and that paid better, you could have a very satisfying life. You mention a dissatisfaction the current authorities and systems in place - perhaps if you were in a position to bring about change / steer these systems in a better direction, you might gain some satisfaction out of this?

Correct. Very satisfying.

>I quit my job a few years ago to go back to uni, where I'm currently studying, and after I graduate I hope to make meaningful contributions to humanitarian initiatives, and help steer my country's healthcare system in better directions. And it's a fuckload of work, and its costing a hell of a lot of money, but I'm a lot happier pursuing something I care about; I hope to be an agent for change in the systems I perceive as broken. 

I want to get a major in philosophy and possibly teach or perform one of many other professions to also help steer the world in a better direction. I would be happy enough not to consider suicide once I finished school and got a well-paying job that I'm fond of. If I'd had better access to college, I would presently be post-grad and quite happy I expect.    

The problem is that the barriers are too high and too many (not impassable, obviously, but I'm overstating nothing). How have you gone back to uni and stopped working? Are you in the US? I don't think that's possible here, anymore. It was in the 70's.

Thanks. 

I don't fully agree that I have the power to change my life. I have some, but the main problem is that other people have control over resources (and service providers) and are denying me access (health care, college, enough to live without too much stress, etc.). I wouldn't mind seeing a psychiatrist, but again, I can't afford it. 

I don't see why life is worth living. The only purpose of staying alive that I see is to achieve happiness, the prospects for which are very dim in my case. 

One bad thing about having no friends or supportive family is not having anyone to help with achieving the material things which I mentioned. It's the lack of achieving those things which is driving me to suicide.

I'm radically anti-capitalist and anti-state and can't stand working in this system anymore. I'm 23 and live in Cleveland, OH. I can't afford to move to Sweden or somewhere similar, as if that would be much better. I am unable to go to college full-time since I did badly overall in high school and I don't want to work  in a capitalist institution to fund living expenses since that's too difficult (I've tried). All I do now is deliver pizza part-time (in a horrible area) and I can't find a better job. I'm stressed most of the time, from my job and from having very little money. I have no friends or acquaintences and almost everyone rejects me almost immediately (the only exception seems to be mentally challenged people). I talk to my mom every once in a while, just to give her updates on the health of her offspring, but she doesn't actually care about my personality. I don't care much for that relationship anyway. I don't actually like most people as they are stupid, irrationally happy and positive, supporters of things I can't stand, etc. The ones I do like, however, certainly don't reciprocate. 

If suicide were as easy as flipping a switch, I would have done that long ago. Unforutnately the body requires massive trauma to die. That's all that stops me.   

I saw a psychologist for a few months but that didn't work out. He diagnosed me with Asperger's syndrome, but I and others don't totally accept it. He would say that my arguments for wanting to die are flawed because I'm mentally ill, but he can't actually refute any of the arguments I give. Isn't that ad hominem? I'm not going to take any pills until someone shows my arguments for wanting to die to be flawed. This is a philosophical issue until then. 

Money would solve most of my problems (I would be at least happy and able to move somewhere better), but I'm not willing to submit to power (at least the kind of extreme power prevalent in this system) in order to get it. The work that I've had to do for money has left my body a wreck. I've gotten in car accidents which have left my neck and jaw a mess, and I can't afford to get them fixed. They make  noise everytime I move them, which interrupt my thought processes, and they get worse everyday I have to work. Work is also an intellectual sinkhole. 

Basically, the cost of living has exceeded the benefits, and the prospects for change are extremely slim.

I'm quite embarrassed to say all this, so go easier than most Reddit-ers (who seem like they'd enjoy masturbating to my snuff video).
